questions.q: Which of the following compound is used as an anti-freeze in automobile radiator ?
questions.solution: **Ethane-1,2-diol** (ethylene glycol) mixed with water lowers the freezing point of the coolant and does not evaporate easily, having a high boiling point.

questions.q: With the Lucas reagent (conc. HCl + anhydrous $\mathrm{ZnCl_2}$), turbidity appears immediately with:
questions.solution:
The Lucas test depends on how easily the alcohol forms a carbocation. A **tertiary** carbocation is the most stable, so tertiary alcohols give the insoluble alkyl chloride **at once**.

Secondary alcohols take about five minutes, and primary alcohols show no turbidity at room temperature.

questions.q: Which one of the following is the Strongest acid ?
questions.solution:
A nitro group at the ortho or para position withdraws electrons by resonance and stabilises the phenoxide ion.

**4-nitrophenol** is the strongest: in 2-nitrophenol an intramolecular hydrogen bond holds the O–H proton back. The meta nitro group acts only inductively, and chlorine is far weaker.

questions.q: Phenol reacts with bromine water to give:
questions.solution:
The –OH group strongly activates the ring. In polar water, bromine substitutes at **all three** ortho and para positions at once, giving a white precipitate of **2,4,6-tribromophenol**.

In a non-polar solvent such as $\mathrm{CS_2}$ at low temperature, monobromination can be achieved instead.

questions.q: The Kolbe reaction of sodium phenoxide with $\mathrm{CO_2}$ followed by acidification gives:
questions.solution:
Sodium phenoxide heated with $\mathrm{CO_2}$ under pressure is carboxylated at the **ortho** position; acidification gives **salicylic acid**, o-hydroxybenzoic acid.

Acetylating salicylic acid gives aspirin.

questions.q: The Reimer–Tiemann reaction of phenol with $\mathrm{CHCl_3}$ and aqueous NaOH gives:
questions.solution:
The reactive species is dichlorocarbene, $\mathrm{:CCl_2}$, made from chloroform and alkali. It attacks the ortho position, and hydrolysis gives **salicylaldehyde**, o-hydroxybenzaldehyde.

Using $\mathrm{CCl_4}$ in place of chloroform gives salicylic acid instead.

questions.q: Ethanol heated with conc. $\mathrm{H_2SO_4}$ at $443\,\mathrm{K}$ gives mainly:
questions.solution:
At $443\,\mathrm{K}$ (170 °C) with excess acid, ethanol undergoes **intramolecular dehydration** to **ethene**.

At the lower temperature of $413\,\mathrm{K}$ with excess alcohol, two molecules lose one water between them and diethyl ether is the main product. The temperature decides the product.

questions.q: Anisole reacts with HI to give:
questions.solution:
The O–$\mathrm{C_6H_5}$ bond has partial double-bond character from resonance, so it does not break. Iodide attacks the **methyl** carbon instead.

$\mathrm{C_6H_5OCH_3} + \mathrm{HI} \rightarrow \mathrm{C_6H_5OH} + \mathrm{CH_3I}$: **phenol and methyl iodide**.

questions.q: Williamson's synthesis prepares an ether by reacting:
options: an alkyl halide with sodium alkoxide
questions.solution:
$\mathrm{R{-}X} + \mathrm{R'ONa} \rightarrow \mathrm{R{-}O{-}R'} + \mathrm{NaX}$, an $S_N2$ reaction.

The alkyl halide should be **primary**: with a tertiary halide the alkoxide acts as a base and elimination gives an alkene instead. It is the method of choice for unsymmetrical ethers.

questions.q: How many of the following are secondary alcohols: propan-2-ol, butan-2-ol, 2-methylpropan-2-ol, cyclohexanol, ethanol?
questions.solution:
Secondary means the carbinol carbon is joined to two carbons.

Propan-2-ol, butan-2-ol and cyclohexanol are secondary: **3**.

2-methylpropan-2-ol is tertiary and ethanol is primary.

questions.q: How many structural isomers, alcohols and ethers together, have the molecular formula $\mathrm{C_3H_8O}$?
questions.solution:
Alcohols: propan-1-ol and propan-2-ol.

Ether: methoxyethane, $\mathrm{CH_3OC_2H_5}$.

Total **3**. Alcohols and ethers of the same formula are functional isomers.

questions.q: How many grams of sodium react completely with $4.6\,\mathrm{g}$ of ethanol? (Na $= 23$, $\mathrm{C_2H_5OH} = 46$.)
questions.solution:
$2\mathrm{C_2H_5OH} + 2\mathrm{Na} \rightarrow 2\mathrm{C_2H_5ONa} + \mathrm{H_2}$: ethanol and sodium react 1 : 1.

Moles of ethanol $= \dfrac{4.6}{46} = 0.1$, so moles of Na $= 0.1$ and mass $= 0.1 \times 23 = \mathbf{2.3\,g}$.

questions.q: What volume of hydrogen, in litres at STP, is released when $0.2\,\mathrm{mol}$ of ethanol reacts completely with sodium? (1 mol of gas at STP $= 22.4\,\mathrm{L}$.)
questions.solution:
Two moles of ethanol release one mole of $\mathrm{H_2}$.

$0.2$ mol of ethanol gives $0.1$ mol of $\mathrm{H_2}$ $= 0.1 \times 22.4 = \mathbf{2.24\,L}$.

questions.q: How many bromine atoms are there in one molecule of the white precipitate formed when phenol reacts with bromine water?
questions.solution: The precipitate is 2,4,6-tribromophenol, $\mathrm{C_6H_2Br_3OH}$: **3** bromine atoms, at both ortho positions and the para position.

questions.q: Describe chemical tests to distinguish between (a) ethanol and phenol, (b) primary, secondary and tertiary alcohols by the Victor Meyer method, and (c) methanol and ethanol.
questions.solution:
**(a) Ethanol and phenol.** Add neutral $\mathrm{FeCl_3}$ solution: phenol gives a **violet** colour, ethanol gives none. Alternatively, bromine water gives phenol a white precipitate of 2,4,6-tribromophenol, while ethanol does not react.

**(b) Victor Meyer method.** The alcohol is converted to the iodide with red P and $\mathrm{I_2}$, then to the nitroalkane with $\mathrm{AgNO_2}$, then treated with nitrous acid and made alkaline.

- **Primary** alcohols give a nitrolic acid, **blood red** in alkali.
- **Secondary** alcohols give a pseudonitrole, **blue**.
- **Tertiary** alcohols have no α-hydrogen on the nitro carbon and stay **colourless**.

**(c) Methanol and ethanol.** The **iodoform test**: warm with $\mathrm{I_2}$ and NaOH. Ethanol contains the $\mathrm{CH_3CH(OH)}{-}$ unit and gives a yellow precipitate of iodoform, $\mathrm{CHI_3}$. Methanol lacks it and gives none.
